svg.title: Chisum: DC1 24 V DC panel, navigation and control, JS8-864 sheet 3 revision 0
svg.text: DC1 · 24 V DC panel, navigation and control
JS8-864 sheet 3 · 24 V direct current · Wheelhouse · register component ELD-03 · fed from DCB (24 v dc board, general service bank)
Navigation sensors, steering and propulsion control, alarms, the red night lighting: on the general service battery, so nothing on it notices a blackout.
FRONT, DOOR OPEN (1 : 4.2 on a 96 dpi screen; the cabinet is 520 × 621 × 210 mm)
X1: terminals 1 to 34 on the lower rail, an earth terminal (green) after each pair.
Gland plate: one gland a cable, in the order of the terminals. PE: the earth bar.
from DCB: feeder to 24 v dc panel, navigation and control
Satellite compass: NAV-11 Satellite compass processor
Navigation data: distributor, network switch, conning display: NAV-09 Navigation data
distributor; NAV-10 Conning display; NAV-14 Navigation network switch
Propulsion remote control: PRP-06 Engine instrument panel; PRP-07 Propulsion control unit, bridge
Bow thruster control: PRP-03 Bow thruster lever
Talkback: INT-02 Public address and talkback panel
Alarm panel, watch alarm, door and ramp panel: ALM-01 Machinery alarm panel; ALM-02 Bridge watch
alarm; ALM-06 Ramp, hatch and watertight door panel
Heading and bearing repeaters, rudder angle indicators: NAV-16 Bearing repeater, port wing;
NAV-17 Bearing repeater, starboard wing; STR-04 Heading repeater; STR-05 Rudder angle indicator,
overhead; STR-06 Rudder angle indicator, console
Wind sensor and display: NAV-13 Wind display
Public address and general alarm, battery supply: INT-01 Public address and general alarm
Night and transitional lighting, binnacle light: NAV-34 Magnetic compass and binnacle; LGT-06
Night light, red, port; LGT-13 Night light, red, starboard; LGT-14 Transitional light
Signalling lamp socket: NLT-21 Daylight signalling lamp

m: the cable's length with its branches and a tenth for bends and making off. Drop: from the switchboard to the farthest consumer. Earth cores go to the terminal after each pair, and from there to the PE bar.
Wall cabinet, sheet steel, 520 mm wide, 210 mm deep, door with a lock, IP44, with mounting plate and gland plate
Switch-disconnector, two-pole, 40 A, 24 V DC, for the incoming feeder
Indicator lamp, supply on, 24 V DC, one for each feeder
Miniature circuit breaker, two-pole, 2 A, for direct current, 24 V
Miniature circuit breaker, two-pole, 4 A, for direct current, 24 V
Miniature circuit breaker, two-pole, 6 A, for direct current, 24 V
Miniature circuit breaker, two-pole, 10 A, for direct current, 24 V
Miniature circuit breaker, two-pole, 16 A, for direct current, 24 V
Earth terminal, green and yellow, on the rail
End stop and end plate for the terminal row
Cable gland, brass, nickel-plated, M20, with locknut and seal
Cable gland, brass, nickel-plated, M25, with locknut and seal
Cable gland, brass, nickel-plated, M50, with locknut and seal
Slotted wiring duct, 40 × 60 mm, with cover
Comb busbar, two-pole, for the row of breakers
Earth bar, copper, with a bolt to the cabinet and to the door
Label, engraved: one for the board, one for each way and each feeder
Circuit list, in a pocket inside the door

The board's contents are the register's: one way for each circuit, each breaker and cable as the register sized them. The cabinet, the devices' form, the terminals and the glands are the yard's own choice (electrical_drawing.py, HARDWARE) and no maker is named.

Both poles of every way are switched and protected: the system is two-wire and insulated from the hull, so a breaker in one pole would leave the other alive. An earth-fault lamp set belongs on the switchboard that feeds the board, not here.

Standards a builder would work to, as the yard recalls them (not read for this sheet): IEC 60092 (electrical installations in ships), IEC 61439 (low-voltage assemblies), IEC 60898-1 and IEC 60947-2 (breakers).
